clue.text: Excitement at topless party

indicators.note: topless means the word for party loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: a carousal is a drunken party or revel

explanation.surface: Someone gets thrilled at a party where the guests have their tops off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the C from CAROUSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is a state of stimulation, a synonym for excitement.

clue.text: A fellow is a looker

parts.note: a don is a university fellow or tutor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that some man is good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, names any strikingly handsome man, a real looker.

clue.text: Recently popped up in metal foundry …

indicators.note: in a down entry, popping up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
in means the letters sit inside the run of words metal foundry

explanation.surface: Something has recently been bursting into view at a metalworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks METALFO out of 'metal foundry', and 'popped up' turns it round to OFLATEM, ignoring the M.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means lately, in the recent past, a synonym for recently.

clue.text: … a foreman with outstanding face protection

parts.note: super means excellent, outstanding
a visor shields the face

explanation.surface: Continuing from the foundry: a foundry boss wearing an excellent face guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the foundry of 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees workers, as a foreman does on a shop floor.

clue.text: Just get the hell out of here!

definitions.meaning: slang for legitimate, lawful or fair, as just is

definitions.text: get the hell out of here!
definitions.meaning: British slang for running away fast

explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate, and to leg it means to flee on foot.

clue.text: Killer game …

definitions.meaning: an executioner who carries out deaths by the rope
the word-guessing pencil game with a gallows drawing

explanation.definitionFit: A hangman executes condemned people, and is also a children's guessing game of letters.

clue.text: Not a breath of fresh air for hoist sail to flap

definitions.text: Not a breath of fresh air

indicators.note: a sail left to flap is shaken about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Raising the sail and letting it flap is hard work for a stale, breathless sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flap' rearranges the letters of 'hoist sail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Halitosis is bad breath, the opposite of a fresh one, defined with playful understatement.

clue.text: Insensitive and stupid to change leader

indicators.note: changing the leader means swapping the first letter of the word for stupid for another

parts.note: dumb means stupid

explanation.surface: Someone is described as both callous and dim, and needing a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change leader' replaces the D of DUMB with N; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means without feeling, so a numb part is insensitive to touch.

clue.text: Gay or straight

definitions.meaning: joking sense: a relationship between one man and another
frank and direct, as in a candid talk between equals

explanation.definitionFit: A man-to-man talk is frank and straight; jokingly the phrase also describes a same-sex male pairing.

clue.text: Given account of island uprising by Hughes

indicators.note: in a down entry, an uprising means the island's letters read upward, backwards

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
Ted Hughes, the English Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A report of a rebellion on an island, written by the poet Hughes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns ARRAN into NARRA; Ted Hughes was Britain's Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrated means told as a story, so a narrated tale has been given an account of.

clue.text: … on the other hand, cut the deck

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, as on the other hand does
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Continuing from 5 across: an alternative is to cut the pack of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cutting a pack of cards, but the deck is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: One seeking or finding nasty old minger

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Either the searcher or the discoverer turns out to be an ugly old person.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, so 'One seeking or' is a prospector; 'nasty' rearranges 'old minger'. Minger is British slang for an unattractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold miner hunts for or, the heraldic name for the yellow metal.

clue.text: Not willing to take right road

indicators.note: to take means the word for not willing holds the letter inside it

parts.note: intestate means dying without having made a will

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant is persuaded to take the correct route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not willing' looks like reluctance, but means having no will: INTESTATE takes R.
explanation.definitionFit: An interstate is a US highway running between states, a kind of road.

clue.text: A gentile backing exercise

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are read in reverse order, back to front

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew

explanation.surface: A non-Jew supports a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns A GOY into YOGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a system of physical postures and breathing practised as exercise.

clue.text: Stripped clue with a pattern

parts.note: the word stripped is the answer to a clue that reads ..., as the letter P put inside STRIPED makes it

explanation.surface: A clue whose disguise has been torn off, leaving its design showing.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, split up, is wordplay whose solution is the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstriped cloth carries a pattern of very thin stripes.

clue.text: Partly dressed, I get treated with insertion of a probe

parts.note: in vest means wearing only a vest, partly dressed

indicators.note: insertion means the letter a is put inside the rearranged letters
treated means processed, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient half undressed is treated with a medical instrument pushed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges I GET to IGTE and 'with insertion of' puts A inside, giving IGATE. Probe is the definition as a verb, not the medical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to look into something closely, which is to investigate it.

clue.text: What they make is drunk and is very silly

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is plastered and behaving very foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges 'and is very'; 'drunk' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vineyards produce wine, which is something that is drunk.

clue.text: O for a chance in the west

indicators.note: O for a means the letter O stands in place of the letter A

parts.note: an accident is a chance happening

explanation.surface: Someone longs for an opportunity out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O for a' swaps the A of ACCIDENT for O; the surface reads like the old exclamation 'O for a...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the western world, the lands of the west.

clue.text: Good money to hear Your Majesty

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

indicators.note: to hear means the word that follows is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: taken as written, then by sound

explanation.surface: Royalty is paid handsomely to listen to petitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' gives EUR as a soundalike of 'your'. 'Your Majesty' looks like a single form of address; the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is impressive splendour, a synonym for majesty.

clue.text: Perhaps not 1 across, ending in chest of drawers

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible arrangement of these letters among many

parts.note: the numeral 1 is read as the letter I

indicators.note: ending in means only the last letter of the word chest is used

explanation.surface: Something that is maybe not exciting ends up in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in' takes the T of 'chest', and 'Perhaps' rearranges NOT I ACROSS with it. 'chest of drawers' is a red herring: drawers are people who draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartoonists draw for a living, so they are drawers in the sense of draughtsmen.

clue.text: Soup that's a mile off maternal dedication

indicators.note: off means the letter for a mile is removed from the phrase

parts.note: to my mum is the dedication a writer might give a mother
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A broth is far from what a book dedicated to mother would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes one M from TO MY MUM. Tom yum is a hot and sour Thai soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom yum is a spicy Thai soup, often made with prawns.

clue.text: Across and behind

parts.note: the first word splits into the letter A and a word meaning angry, and that angry word's synonym after A also means behind on a ship

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Across' into A and CROSS; cross means angry, or STERN, so A STERN; 'behind' is the meaning, as at the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for behind or at the back of a ship.

clue.text: Take regular winnings in pubs

indicators.note: taking regular letters means picking every other letter of winnings

explanation.surface: A gambler collects the usual winnings in the bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take regular' picks the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'winnings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are public houses, places where drink is sold.

clue.text: Cryptic compiler's to start in earnest

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so compiler's means my

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for earnest

parts.note: earnest means serious

indicators.note: to start means just the first letter of the word to is used

explanation.surface: A crossword setter announces they are about to begin in all seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks of themselves in the first person, so 'compiler's' means 'my'; 'Cryptic' looks like a description of the crossword but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cryptic is obscure or puzzling, which is mysterious.

clue.text: Thanks sex deviant, with death a certainty

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you

indicators.note: deviant means departing from the norm, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A grateful remark to a sexual deviant facing certain execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviant' rearranges SEX into XES. The definition alludes to Benjamin Franklin's line that nothing is certain except death and taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin's saying pairs taxes with death as life's only certainties.

clue.text: Somehow justified excluding unhealthy diets at the peak

indicators.note: somehow means arranged in some unspecified way, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Somehow, cutting out bad diets seemed worth it at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding unhealthy diets' means the letters of DIETS, in any order, come out of JUSTIFIED, leaving J U F I, which 'Somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuji is Japan's highest mountain, a famous volcanic peak.

clue.text: Will manager put old flame before old money and verbal subterfuge?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
the ecu was an old French coin

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: tricks are subterfuge, acts of deception

explanation.surface: A question of whether an estate's executor puts a former lover ahead of inherited wealth and deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal' gives TRIX as a soundalike of TRICKS. 'Will' is a testament, not desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An executrix is a woman appointed to carry out the terms of a will.

clue.text: Recipient's old man with evil eye

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: evil means corrupted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipient is described as a father with the evil eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evil' rearranges EYE into YEE; 'evil eye' looks like a fixed phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the person to whom money is paid, its recipient.

clue.text: Roots of revolution and counter-revolution overlapping

indicators.note: overlapping means the two words share their meeting letter, so one copy is dropped

parts.note: a turn is one revolution

indicators.note: counter means running against, so the word for a revolution is read backwards

parts.note: a spin is a revolution

explanation.surface: The origins of a revolution and the backlash against it overlap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' turns SPIN into NIPS; 'overlapping' merges the N ending TURN with the N starting NIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips are edible root vegetables, so they are roots.

clue.text: Maiden's crazy for musician

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the word with its s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A young woman is wild about a player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges MAIDENS, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideman is a supporting musician in a band or orchestra.
